title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife

evidence_packet.title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife
evidence_packet.lead: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
evidence_packet.summary: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters and drinking stations for insects and animals beside it Work at the site in Urmston, Greater Manchester, has been made possible with the help of local businesses "It's been absolutely thriving with wildlife, said Lisa Smith, allotment treasurer. "We've even had a fox up there. It's just been such an incredible achievement to create this." Smith added: "Since World War Two, pollinators have been under threat due to the loss of 97 per cent of wildflower meadows in the UK, so we thought we really need to try and rectify that." Mick Heery, chairman of Brookfield Allotment, told BBC Radio Manchester sustainability also plays an important role in their work

evidence_packet.title: All eyes on Greater Manchester ahead of mayoral election
evidence_packet.lead: Voters in Greater Manchester will go to the polls on Thursday to choose Andy Burnham's successor as mayor
evidence_packet.summary: Voters in Greater Manchester will go to the polls on Thursday to choose Andy Burnham's successor as mayor
evidence_packet.evidence_text: All eyes on Greater Manchester ahead of mayoral election - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Voters will head to the polls on Thursday By Professor Andrew Russell University of Liverpool and former head of politics at the University of Manchester Published 1 hour ago Voters across Greater Manchester will head to the polls on Thursday to elect a new mayor for the city region. It is a very important role - only the prime minister and the mayor of London have more power in English politics. After Andy Burnham was elected in the Makerfield by-election last month, paving his way to Downing Street, he automatically had to resign as Greater Manchester's mayor. Labour's candidate to replace him is the current leader of Manchester City Council, Bev Craig. She faces a tougher task in the other nine boroughs. While Labour has often won elections across the city region, the party's level of support varies. For instance, at a time when Labour held 95 of 96 council seats on Manchester City Council, eight of the 10 Greater Manchester boroughs voted leave in the 2016 Brexit referendum. This may well give hope to Reform UK, for example. Craig, who has led the city council since 2021, has filled big shoes before. Her predecessor, Sir Richard Leese, was in charge for more than a quarter of a century, taking in an era including Britpop, the 2002 Commonwealth Games and the soaring city skyscape. Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor for Greater Manchester in 2017 and was re-elected twice. Each time Burnham outpolled his party, gaining a majority of votes in all boroughs. In 2017 he even managed to defeat his Conservative opponent - the leader of Trafford Council - in his own backyard. title: Probe into Bickershaw illegal dump's toxic chemicals claim

evidence_packet.title: Probe into Bickershaw illegal dump's toxic chemicals claim
evidence_packet.lead: About 25,000 tonnes of toxic waste remains at the site of a former scrapyard
evidence_packet.summary: About 25,000 tonnes of toxic waste remains at the site of a former scrapyard
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Probe into Bickershaw illegal dump's toxic chemicals claim - BBC News Image caption, The Bolton House Road site is currently sealed off and is subject to a closure notice By Chris Gee Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 26 July 2026 The Environment Agency (EA) has said it will "carefully consider" claims chemicals posing a health risk have been found at an illegal dump. Approximately 25,000 tonnes of toxic waste remains at the site of a former scrapyard on Bolton House Road in the village of Bickershaw, in Wigan. It follows an investigation by Sky News , external , which has been working with scientists to conduct testing of air, water and soil at the site. A criminal investigation is continuing to find out who was responsible for dumping the rubbish at the former scrapyard, which was discovered last summer. A 58-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested in May on suspicion of environmental, fraud, and money laundering offences. He was later released on conditional bail. 'Own evidence' An "ocean of rubbish" emerged last summer, and later a week-long fire saw tonnes of waste burned, emitting dangerous fumes and forcing nearby schools to close. The Bolton House Road site is currently sealed off and subject to a closure notice. The government said people should never enter due to the potential harm. In March, the government said it would directly fund the clean-up, with the EA given more powers to enforce waste crime. However, five months after it was announced, the dump is still there. Following the publication of the test results, an EA spokesperson said: "Our scientists will carefully consider these findings alongside our own evidence. title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'

evidence_packet.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
evidence_packet.lead: Speaking exclusively to the BBC, the prime minister says he had a good first conversation with the US president and insists "you have to defend your own national interest"
evidence_packet.summary: Speaking exclusively to the BBC, the prime minister says he had a good first conversation with the US president and insists "you have to defend your own national interest"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg Published 26 July 2026 Andy Burnham says he would be prepared to call out Donald Trump to defend Britain's "national interest before anything else" if it is the right thing to do, in his first major interview as prime minister Speaking exclusively to the BBC, Burnham said he had had a good first exchange with Trump, finding him to be "really warm" But asked twice if he would trust the US president, he did not say, answering, "it's a changing world isn't it, and you just obviously have to call things as they develop" In the interview, to be broadcast in full on Monday, he said: "I can't at any point say that I won't take a different opinion from him [Trump], that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain." title: People's History Museum to display rare Peterloo massacre jug

evidence_packet.title: People's History Museum to display rare Peterloo massacre jug
evidence_packet.lead: The jug commemorating the 1819 Peterloo massacre will be displayed at the People's History Museum
evidence_packet.summary: The jug commemorating the 1819 Peterloo massacre will be displayed at the People's History Museum
evidence_packet.evidence_text: People's History Museum to display rare Peterloo massacre jug - BBC News Image source, People's History Museum handout Image caption, Professor Robert Poole said the commemorative jug adds "a new dimension to the story of Peterloo" By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 26 July 2026 An "exceptionally rare" jug commemorating the Peterloo Massacre is to go on display in Manchester. Thousands of people gathered in the city on 16 August 1819 to take part in a peaceful protest calling for political reform and more voting rights. As many as 18 protesters are believed to have been killed, with many more injured, after soldiers were ordered to arrest the demonstration's leaders and put an end to the protest. Jenny Mabbott, from the People's History Museum, said the jug - which will be on display from 1 August to 3 January - was a "direct link to one of the defining moments in the history of democracy in Britain". The jug was acquired thanks to support from the Art Fund, the national charity for museums and galleries. Experts believe the jug was made in the years following the massacre and that it reflected the escalating public anger felt in its aftermath, the People's History Museum said. It features a map of the site where the Peterloo Massacre took place when yeomanry charged into a crowd of about 60,000 people. Although the jugs would have been produced on a commercial scale, no other examples of this design have been identified, making this one exceptionally rare. It will join significant Peterloo objects already on display at the museum including yeomanry sabres, a commemorative handkerchief, and a cane carried by one of the protesters. title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.summary: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?

evidence_packet.title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester goes to the polls on 30 July, but what powers does the region's mayor hold?
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester goes to the polls on 30 July, but what powers does the region's mayor hold?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? The role of mayor was created as part of a law passed in 2016, one of a number of big pieces of devolution legislation brought in by the Conservatives after taking power in 2010 In a 2012 referendum, Manchester rejected having a directly-elected city mayor, along with eight other major cities, but the decision to have a regional or metropolitan mayor was directly negotiated between the government and the 10 Greater Manchester councils Andy Burnham, who left Parliament to stand for the role, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the first mayoral election in 2017 and won, taking 63.4% of the vote

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police are investigating a hoax threat made by a 14-year-old boy to an aircraft heading to Manchester Airport NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons were scrambled from Lincolnshire on Friday to intercept the Qatar Airways flight in response, the Ministry of Defence confirmed The aircraft landed safely and there was no threat to passengers or crew, Greater Manchester Police confirmed The teenager from Bolton, who was not on the flight, has been identified and is "assisting officers with their inquiries", police said Ch Insp Gary Homa said: "This type of behaviour is completely unacceptable. evidence_packet.title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife
evidence_packet.lead: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters
evidence_packet.summary: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters and drinking stations for insects and animals beside it Work at the site in Urmston, Greater Manchester, has been made possible with the help of local businesses "It's been absolutely thriving with wildlife, said Lisa Smith, allotment treasurer. "We've even had a fox up there. It's just been such an incredible achievement to create this." evidence_packet.summary: An "exceptionally rare" jug commemorating the Peterloo Massacre is to go on display in Manchester Thousands of people gathered in the city on 16 August 1819 to take part in a peaceful protest calling for political reform and more voting rights As many as 18 protesters are believe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An "exceptionally rare" jug commemorating the Peterloo Massacre is to go on display in Manchester Thousands of people gathered in the city on 16 August 1819 to take part in a peaceful protest calling for political reform and more voting rights As many as 18 protesters are believed to have been killed, with many more injured, after soldiers were ordered to arrest the demonstration's leaders and put an end to the protest Jenny Mabbott, from the People's History Museum, said the jug - which will be on display from 1 August to 3 January - was a "direct link to one of the defining moments in the history of democracy in Britain" The jug was acquired thanks to support from the Art Fund, the national charity for museums and galleries Experts believe the jug was made in the years following the massacre and that it reflected the escalating public anger felt in its aftermath, the People's History Museum said

title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.summary: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they wil
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? The role of mayor was created as part of a law passed in 2016, one of a number of big pieces of devolution legislation brought in by the Conservatives after taking power in 2010 In a 2012 referendum, Manchester rejected having a directly-elected city mayor, along with eight other major cities, but the decision to have a regional or metropolitan mayor was directly negotiated between the government and the 10 Greater Manchester councils Andy Burnham, who left Parliament to stand for the role, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the first mayoral election in 2017 and won, taking 63.4% of the vote

title: Police question boy, 14, over Manchester Airport aircraft hoax threat

evidence_packet.title: Police question boy, 14, over Manchester Airport aircraft hoax threat
evidence_packet.lead: Police are investigating a hoax threat made by a 14-year-old boy to an aircraft heading to Manchester Airport NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons
evidence_packet.summary: Police are investigating a hoax threat made by a 14-year-old boy to an aircraft heading to Manchester Airport NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police are investigating a hoax threat made by a 14-year-old boy to an aircraft heading to Manchester Airport NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons were scrambled from Lincolnshire on Friday to intercept the Qatar Airways flight in response, the Ministry of Defence confirmed The aircraft landed safely and there was no threat to passengers or crew, Greater Manchester Police confirmed The teenager from Bolton, who was not on the flight, has been identified and is "assisting officers with their inquiries", police said Ch Insp Gary Homa said: "This type of behaviour is completely unacceptable. The safety of the public is always our top priority and every report of this nature is treated extremely seriously

evidence_packet.title: Salford dole demo site nominated for heritage protection list
evidence_packet.lead: The site of a protest against dole cuts in the 1930s by jobless workers who clashed with police has been nominated for "protected heritage" status in a city Bexley Square in Salford is among places including pubs, historic churches, bridges, war memorials and even a bingo hall co
evidence_packet.summary: The site of a protest against dole cuts in the 1930s by jobless workers who clashed with police has been nominated for "protected heritage" status in a city Bexley Square in Salford is among places including pubs, historic churches, bridges, war memorials and even a bingo hall co
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The site of a protest against dole cuts in the 1930s by jobless workers who clashed with police has been nominated for "protected heritage" status in a city Bexley Square in Salford is among places including pubs, historic churches, bridges, war memorials and even a bingo hall considered by Salford Council The Battle of Bexley Square saw around 10,000 trade unionists protesting outside Salford Town Hall on 1 October 1931 against the introduction of the coalition government's "means test" for unemployment benefit A local heritage asset designation must be taken into consideration during planning applications, meaning architects are expected to design buildings reflecting the existing area The means test - where people had to prove they were in need - was introduced by Ramsay MacDonald's coalition government in order to stabilise the British economy, following the 1929 Wall Street crash The protest by the Salford branch of the National Unemployed Workers' Movement was meant to see them hold a march and hand in a petition at the town hall

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Major engineering work on a key stretch of the Manchester Metrolink network will be worth the inconvenience, transport bosses have said Work started on 16 July to replace one mile (1.6km) of track - some of which is more than 30 years old - and continues until 2 August with no trams available on the Eccles, Trafford Centre and Altrincham lines It is part of a wider £150m programme to improve 6km of track, which will finish next year However some councillors say replacement bus services, especially around Altincham and Timperley, are "not fit for purpose" - Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) said it is "strengthening" the service Lib Dem councillor Ulrich Savary, who represents Broadheath ward on Trafford Council, said he was inundated with complaints about the replacement bus service last week with people alleging some services have not appeared at all. Others are said to have taken three times the lengt Savary said: "I had quite a lot of complaints although there has been some improvement this week."

evidence_packet.lead: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been miss

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been missing for four days. Police say Kiralee was last seen on Richmond Drive, in Leigh , at around 6.10pm on Thursday (July 23) Kiralee is described as a white woman, who was last seen wearing a grey/blue top and black leggings, with white socks over the top. She also wore white New Balance trainers and was seen carrying both a Steve Madden bag and a small Gucci bag Greater Manchester Police issued an urgent appeal for help finding her this morning (Monday). A force spokesperson said: "Officers are becoming increasingly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well." A photo of Kiralee was issued as part of the appeal. Anyone who sees Kiralee or has information on her whereabouts is urged to come forward as soon as possible Information can be passed on to GMP by calling 101, quoting log number 3270-230726. In an emergency situation, dial 999

All my family have known me to always be just obsessed with paper and drawing. It seemed natural that, after leaving school with GCSEs in art and graphic design, Paige went on to study textiles and graphics at college before later moving to London to pursue a textiles degree After graduating, she got a placement at a design company in Yorkshire that created cards and stationery for clients, including Marks & Spencer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Manchester is building more homes than the whole of Greater London The city's housing boom is moving forward. News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 13:16, 24 Jul 2026 Updated 06:12, 27 Jul 2026 View 2 Images Manchester has major regene Manchester is building more new homes than the whole of Greater London, the council has said - but the claim has been disputed by the mayor of London Figures published by Manchester council this week showed a total of 4,766 homes were built in the city in 2025/26 City leaders in Manchester said this is more than all of the Greater London area, which managed to build 4,261 homes in the same period London’s housing data was taken from London Datastore, a website by the Greater London Authority But pointing to other data, the mayor of London’s office said the city has in fact built more homes than Manchester

title: Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding'

evidence_packet.lead: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding' She made a direct plea to the new Prime Minister Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 22:02, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Saz Burwin's video on TikTok Andy Burnham has acknowledge
evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding' She made a direct plea to the new Prime Minister Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 22:02, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Saz Burwin's video on TikTok Andy Burnham has acknowledge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding' She made a direct plea to the new Prime Minister Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 22:02, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Saz Burwin's video on TikTok Andy Burnham has acknowledged a plea from a bride not to 'ruin' her wedding which is happening in the shadow of the new Number 10 North The government's new northern headquarters, currently based in Heron House facing Albert Square in Manchester city centre, was officially opened by the new Prime Minister who made his first visit on Friday (July 24) He is expected to work from the new hub at least once a week whilst other cabinet ministers are expected to work there on a regular basis There was a police presence outside the building, which also houses GCHQ's North West base, throughout the week. This then ramped up on Friday with a large police presence including armed officers patrolling the area around it Mr Burnham's security convoy was driven straight into the building in the morning and metal fencing was also erected around the front entrance. He did however come out to greet crowds who had gathered hoping to catch a glimpse of him, telling them: "I love you Manchester."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Moor fires still burning despite rain with crews working 'tirelessly' say fire service chiefs Responses to the major incidents are continuing News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 21:20, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Firefighters working on Tintwistle Rain has helped crews battling the huge wildfires on the moors above Greater Manchester but they are still burning, fire chiefs have said tonight Crews have been tackling the fire near Dovestone Reservoir, in Greenfield, Oldham, since Saturday, July 11, with a nearby area of moorland at Swineshaw, near Glossop, also alight The operation to contain another nearby moorland blaze, close to the village of Tintwistle, is also continuing, forcing the closure of the A628 Woodhead Pass The area covered by both fires is said to be equivalent to 1,250 football pitches Following a prolonged dry spell which has made firefighting efforts extremely challenging, the region saw its first rain overnight and into today (Sunday, July 26)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Woodley 'For me, it's a death sentence - but what am I going to do?' Stockport County FC and the council have been criticised, with concerns from some plans could 'destroy' the community News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 16:34, 26 Jul 2026 V People living in a Stockport town fear a ‘massive part’ of their lives will be lost, leaving their community ‘destroyed’. One pensioner said: “For me it’s a death sentence, but what am I going to do?” Following a decision earlier this year, Stockport council is selling the freehold for the major sports facility Stockport Sports Village to Stockport County Education Pathway Limited (SCEP), a company linked to the local sports club. The club was privately developed in 2012 by Wo The Woodley site was later bought by Life Leisure – a Stockport council-owned company – providing sports and leisure facilities in the borough, in 2018 and it was later bought by the town hall. No sale price has been revealed, but the council considered the sale will cover borrow Stockport County’s takeover of the site has meant the Life Leisure gym on the site will close in December 2026. While there will still be access for community football, the move is driving fears amongst some in the local community arguing it was ‘a deal done underhand behind clos Several people in the community said the decision to sell the site took them completely by surprise in February 2026, including that even staff did not know it was happening. It is understood those will now either transfer to the football club or other Life Leisure roles

She is being supported by social services after she said she was abused Manchester council has apologised and said Annie should never have been placed in the property. Deputy council leader Tracey Rawlins said the case was an exception, but that ‘significant lessons have been learned’ Annie is being supported by Greater Manchester mayoral candidate Sian Astley. It comes as the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) decided not to recommission the Women in Safe Homes or WISH scheme The temporary scheme was aimed to support women experiencing homelessness or abuse and help them get back on their feet

These included gun-shaped toys, yoghurts and 12 pairs of scissors. Travellers are reminded to follow the Civil Aviation Authority's rules for hand luggage which includes a 100ml View 2 Images Manchester Airport is expecting its busiest summer on record (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been missing for four days. Police say Kiralee was last seen on Richmond Drive, in Leigh , at around 6.10pm on Thursday (July 23) Kiralee is described as a white woman, who was last seen wearing a grey/blue top and black leggings, with white socks over the top. She also wore white New Balance trainers and was seen carrying both a Steve Madden bag and a small Gucci bag Greater Manchester Police issued an urgent appeal for help finding her this morning (Monday). A force spokesperson said: "Officers are becoming increasingly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well." A photo of Kiralee was issued as part of the appeal. Anyone who sees Kiralee or has information on her whereabouts is urged to come forward as soon as possible Information can be passed on to GMP by calling 101, quoting log number 3270-230726. In an emergency situation, dial 999

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police 'Shut the f*** up... enough of that racist s***': How a detainee's vile abuse landed three cops in hot water A drunken suspect launched a tirade of racist abuse at three police officers as he was being taken to a police stati News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:11, 27 Jul 2026 Updated 06:17, 27 Jul 2026 A cop who stopped filming when a fellow officer confronted a racist detainee in the back of a police van has been sacked in disgrace Probationary officer Pc William Byers 'deliberately' switched off his body-worn camera out of a 'misguided sense of loyalty' when Sgt David Rothwell tackled handcuffed suspect Borwar Ahmed, a Greater Manchester Police misconduct panel ruled Moments earlier Ahmed had launched a drunken tirade of foul racist abuse at a third officer PC Brendan Colley, who was driving the van Ahmed, whose hands were covered in blood, repeatedly called Pc Colley a 'monkey' amid other racist slurs, while he referred to the other officers as 'white b****' and threatened to rape their children and mothers In the midst of the abuse Sgt Rothwell told PC Colley to stop the van, then got out and climbed into the 'cage' alongside Ahmed. Ever since she was a young child, Paige has loved drawing and would spend her pocket money collecting pens and stationery The 35-year-old told the Manchester Evening News : "I'd go in every weekend, I'd buy diaries, notebooks – never writing in them because they're too precious to write in, so I'd just collect everything. All my family have known me to always be just obsessed with paper and drawing. It seemed natural that, after leaving school with GCSEs in art and graphic design, Paige went on to study textiles and graphics at college before later moving to London to pursue a textiles degree After graduating, she got a placement at a design company in Yorkshire that created cards and stationery for clients, including Marks & Spencer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding' She made a direct plea to the new Prime Minister Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 22:02, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Saz Burwin's video on TikTok Andy Burnham has acknowledged a plea from a bride not to 'ruin' her wedding which is happening in the shadow of the new Number 10 North The government's new northern headquarters, currently based in Heron House facing Albert Square in Manchester city centre, was officially opened by the new Prime Minister who made his first visit on Friday (July 24) He is expected to work from the new hub at least once a week whilst other cabinet ministers are expected to work there on a regular basis There was a police presence outside the building, which also houses GCHQ's North West base, throughout the week. This then ramped up on Friday with a large police presence including armed officers patrolling the area around it Mr Burnham's security convoy was driven straight into the building in the morning and metal fencing was also erected around the front entrance. He did however come out to greet crowds who had gathered hoping to catch a glimpse of him, telling them: "I love you Manchester."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Moor fires still burning despite rain with crews working 'tirelessly' say fire service chiefs Responses to the major incidents are continuing News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 21:20, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Firefighters working on Tintwistle Rain has helped crews battling the huge wildfires on the moors above Greater Manchester but they are still burning, fire chiefs have said tonight Crews have been tackling the fire near Dovestone Reservoir, in Greenfield, Oldham, since Saturday, July 11, with a nearby area of moorland at Swineshaw, near Glossop, also alight The operation to contain another nearby moorland blaze, close to the village of Tintwistle, is also continuing, forcing the closure of the A628 Woodhead Pass The area covered by both fires is said to be equivalent to 1,250 football pitches Following a prolonged dry spell which has made firefighting efforts extremely challenging, the region saw its first rain overnight and into today (Sunday, July 26)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Woodley 'For me, it's a death sentence - but what am I going to do?' Stockport County FC and the council have been criticised, with concerns from some plans could 'destroy' the community News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 16:34, 26 Jul 2026 V People living in a Stockport town fear a ‘massive part’ of their lives will be lost, leaving their community ‘destroyed’. One pensioner said: “For me it’s a death sentence, but what am I going to do?” Following a decision earlier this year, Stockport council is selling the freehold for the major sports facility Stockport Sports Village to Stockport County Education Pathway Limited (SCEP), a company linked to the local sports club. The club was privately developed in 2012 by Wo The Woodley site was later bought by Life Leisure – a Stockport council-owned company – providing sports and leisure facilities in the borough, in 2018 and it was later bought by the town hall. No sale price has been revealed, but the council considered the sale will cover borrow Stockport County’s takeover of the site has meant the Life Leisure gym on the site will close in December 2026. While there will still be access for community football, the move is driving fears amongst some in the local community arguing it was ‘a deal done underhand behind clos Several people in the community said the decision to sell the site took them completely by surprise in February 2026, including that even staff did not know it was happening. It is understood those will now either transfer to the football club or other Life Leisure roles

evidence_packet.title: Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester Ten years on GMP is still dogged by IT issues View 5 Images Hyperlocal crime is provided by every force in Britain - except GMP (Image: News Richard Ault and Neal Ke
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester Ten years on GMP is still dogged by IT issues View 5 Images Hyperlocal crime is provided by every force in Britain - except GMP (Image: News Richard Ault and Neal Ke
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester Ten years on GMP is still dogged by IT issues View 5 Images Hyperlocal crime is provided by every force in Britain - except GMP (Image: News Richard Ault and Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:34, 25 Jul 2026 Updated 16:54, 25 Jul 2026 Sadly, everyone knows Piccadilly Gardens remains a maelstrom of criminality. Brazen drug dealing, violence and robbery tarnish the area and have made it a dangerous cut-through In 2023, a police operation was launched there. It did have an impact, with 14 arrests in its first week. But the problems persist as the gardens await a radical redesign Yet, according to Greater Manchester Police neighbourhood data, just four crimes were committed in Piccadilly Gardens in the last 12 months Despite massive improvements by the force amid a drastic turnaround in performance - having been put into special measures - people across Greater Manchester still can't find out how many crimes are being committed where they live For example, according to the crime statistics section of the Greater Manchester Police site, four crimes were recorded in Piccadilly Gardens in the past year; three in Moss side; and none at all in Longsight

evidence_packet.lead: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been miss
evidence_packet.summary: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been miss
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leigh Urgent appeal issued to find woman, 21, missing for four days She was last seen in Leigh News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:45, 27 Jul 2026 View Image Kiralee is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a 21-year-old woman who has been missing for four days. Police say Kiralee was last seen on Richmond Drive, in Leigh , at around 6.10pm on Thursday (July 23) Kiralee is described as a white woman, who was last seen wearing a grey/blue top and black leggings, with white socks over the top. She also wore white New Balance trainers and was seen carrying both a Steve Madden bag and a small Gucci bag Greater Manchester Police issued an urgent appeal for help finding her this morning (Monday). A force spokesperson said: "Officers are becoming increasingly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well." A photo of Kiralee was issued as part of the appeal. Anyone who sees Kiralee or has information on her whereabouts is urged to come forward as soon as possible Information can be passed on to GMP by calling 101, quoting log number 3270-230726. In an emergency situation, dial 999

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'I never returned from maternity leave after starting £100k a year business from my garage' Wigan mum, Paige Calland, had always wanted to start her own business but had never found the time until she was furloughed during the pandemic News Lee A mum found the courage to follow her dream while furloughed during the coronavirus pandemic - making £100k in sales during her second year in business Paige Calland lives in Leigh with her husband, Scott, and their daughters, Pia, five, and one-year-old Dora. Ever since she was a young child, Paige has loved drawing and would spend her pocket money collecting pens and stationery The 35-year-old told the Manchester Evening News : "I'd go in every weekend, I'd buy diaries, notebooks – never writing in them because they're too precious to write in, so I'd just collect everything. All my family have known me to always be just obsessed with paper and drawing. It seemed natural that, after leaving school with GCSEs in art and graphic design, Paige went on to study textiles and graphics at college before later moving to London to pursue a textiles degree After graduating, she got a placement at a design company in Yorkshire that created cards and stationery for clients, including Marks & Spencer

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham responds after bride begs Prime Minister 'please don't ruin my wedding' She made a direct plea to the new Prime Minister Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 22:02, 26 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Saz Burwin's video on TikTok Andy Burnham has acknowledged a plea from a bride not to 'ruin' her wedding which is happening in the shadow of the new Number 10 North The government's new northern headquarters, currently based in Heron House facing Albert Square in Manchester city centre, was officially opened by the new Prime Minister who made his first visit on Friday (July 24) He is expected to work from the new hub at least once a week whilst other cabinet ministers are expected to work there on a regular basis There was a police presence outside the building, which also houses GCHQ's North West base, throughout the week. This then ramped up on Friday with a large police presence including armed officers patrolling the area around it Mr Burnham's security convoy was driven straight into the building in the morning and metal fencing was also erected around the front entrance. He did however come out to greet crowds who had gathered hoping to catch a glimpse of him, telling them: "I love you Manchester."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Council The abuse survivor dumped in a flat 'worse than a pigsty' She said she wouldn't wish it on her worst enemy View 5 Images 'What I have been put into is disgusting' (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News) News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 15:47, 26 Jul 2026 Updated 16:56, 26 Jul 2026 An abuse survivor put in a flat ‘worse than a pigsty’ said she would not wish the ‘disgusting’ conditions on her worst enemy Annie - not her real name - said she endured a range of issues with the property, which she has been told was ‘condemned’. She is being supported by social services after she said she was abused Manchester council has apologised and said Annie should never have been placed in the property. Deputy council leader Tracey Rawlins said the case was an exception, but that ‘significant lessons have been learned’ Annie is being supported by Greater Manchester mayoral candidate Sian Astley. It comes as the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) decided not to recommission the Women in Safe Homes or WISH scheme The temporary scheme was aimed to support women experiencing homelessness or abuse and help them get back on their feet

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Woodley 'For me, it's a death sentence - but what am I going to do?' Stockport County FC and the council have been criticised, with concerns from some plans could 'destroy' the community News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 16:34, 26 Jul 2026 V People living in a Stockport town fear a ‘massive part’ of their lives will be lost, leaving their community ‘destroyed’. One pensioner said: “For me it’s a death sentence, but what am I going to do?” Following a decision earlier this year, Stockport council is selling the freehold for the major sports facility Stockport Sports Village to Stockport County Education Pathway Limited (SCEP), a company linked to the local sports club. The club was privately developed in 2012 by Wo The Woodley site was later bought by Life Leisure – a Stockport council-owned company – providing sports and leisure facilities in the borough, in 2018 and it was later bought by the town hall. No sale price has been revealed, but the council considered the sale will cover borrow Stockport County’s takeover of the site has meant the Life Leisure gym on the site will close in December 2026. While there will still be access for community football, the move is driving fears amongst some in the local community arguing it was ‘a deal done underhand behind clos Several people in the community said the decision to sell the site took them completely by surprise in February 2026, including that even staff did not know it was happening. It is understood those will now either transfer to the football club or other Life Leisure roles

On the Silver Lions team will be BBC presenter Mike Sweeney. who will be getting his fifth international call-up for the squad View 7 Images Mike Sweeney is hoping England's over 75s for whom he plays right full back will beat Germany in the match in Oldham The radio star, frontman for punk band the Salford Jets, made is debut for the team in 2024 against Wales. evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester Ten years on GMP is still dogged by IT issues View 5 Images Hyperlocal crime is provided by every force in Britain - except GMP (Image: News Richard Ault and Neal Ke
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Why it appears no crimes have been committed in neighbourhoods across Greater Manchester Ten years on GMP is still dogged by IT issues View 5 Images Hyperlocal crime is provided by every force in Britain - except GMP (Image: News Richard Ault and Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:34, 25 Jul 2026 Updated 16:54, 25 Jul 2026 Sadly, everyone knows Piccadilly Gardens remains a maelstrom of criminality. Brazen drug dealing, violence and robbery tarnish the area and have made it a dangerous cut-through In 2023, a police operation was launched there. It did have an impact, with 14 arrests in its first week. But the problems persist as the gardens await a radical redesign Yet, according to Greater Manchester Police neighbourhood data, just four crimes were committed in Piccadilly Gardens in the last 12 months Despite massive improvements by the force amid a drastic turnaround in performance - having been put into special measures - people across Greater Manchester still can't find out how many crimes are being committed where they live For example, according to the crime statistics section of the Greater Manchester Police site, four crimes were recorded in Piccadilly Gardens in the past year; three in Moss side; and none at all in Longsight

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 19 June 2026 at 1:43pm Andy Burnham has been mayor of Greater Manchester for almost a decade. Credit: PA Images Andy Burnham’s historic victory in the Makerfield by-election sets off a rapid chain reaction for both Greater Manchester and the wider UK political landscape A metro mayor cannot simultaneously serve as an MP, a clear legal and electoral process is now underway to find someone new to take on the role Andy Burnham has won a seat as an MP - but can he still be the Mayor of Greater Manchester? No. Andy Burnham cannot be mayor and a member of parliament. He had seven days - from the moment of his election - to resign from the post which he has held for almost a decade He handed in his resignation on 19 June - triggering the process of the by-election Burnham cannot do both jobs because the Mayor of Greater Manchester holds Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) powers and UK law strictly dictates that the office holder cannot simultaneously serve as an MP

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It runs from Saturday 25 July until Monday 31 August Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A free detective-themed trail is coming to Altrincham town centre this summer, challenging families to solve a football-inspired whodunnit before the new season kicks off The Case of the Missing League Ball, launched by Altrincham BID, runs from Saturday 25 July until Monday 31 August The self-guided trail asks budding detectives to work out who has stolen the brand-new league ball ahead of the football season Clues are hidden along a route through the town centre, with each one revealing something about the mystery thief. Participants eliminate suspects one by one until only the culprit remains - discovering some of Altrincham's shops and businesses along the way Taking part is free. Families can download the Visit Altrincham App and head to the Tours section to start the trail. A list of suspects is available in the app, or as a printed Suspect List from Everyman Altrincham

evidence_packet.summary: NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons were scrambled from Lincolnshire on Friday to intercept the Qatar Airways flight in response, the Ministry of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, received the threat at about 18:00 BST on Friday, and police responded alongside the RAF and airport authorities RAF Typhoons were scrambled from Lincolnshire on Friday to intercept the Qatar Airways flight in response, the Ministry of Defence confirmed The aircraft landed safely and there was no threat to passengers or crew, Greater Manchester Police confirmed The teenager from Bolton, who was not on the flight, has been identified and is "assisting officers with their inquiries", police said Ch Insp Gary Homa said: "This type of behaviour is completely unacceptable. The safety of the public is always our top priority and every report of this nature is treated extremely seriously "Hoax calls can cause significant disruption, divert vital emergency service resources and create unnecessary concern for passengers, crew and the wider public," he said

title: Two Rochdale park sex attacks may be linked, say police

evidence_packet.title: Two Rochdale park sex attacks may be linked, say police
evidence_packet.lead: At 06:15 BST, officers received a report a woman had been sexually assaulted in Broadfield Park, Rochdale, by a man she did not know A second sexual assault report was made at 08:38 by a woman who was attacked in Milnrow Memorial Park, again by a man she did not know Both victims
evidence_packet.summary: At 06:15 BST, officers received a report a woman had been sexually assaulted in Broadfield Park, Rochdale, by a man she did not know A second sexual assault report was made at 08:38 by a woman who was attacked in Milnrow Memorial Park, again by a man she did not know Both victims
evidence_packet.evidence_text: At 06:15 BST, officers received a report a woman had been sexually assaulted in Broadfield Park, Rochdale, by a man she did not know A second sexual assault report was made at 08:38 by a woman who was attacked in Milnrow Memorial Park, again by a man she did not know Both victims have provided a similar description of the suspect, who was a black male believed to have been wearing a three piece suit or smart black clothes and a dark coat and carrying a briefcase Greater Manchester Police have identified CCTV footage of a man matching the description in the Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale town centre, who was seen leaving the venue at about 05:00 Detectives are appealing for anyone who may have seen a man matching this description, or who has CCTV, dashcam, doorbell, or mobile phone footage from the town centre, Broadfield Park or Milnrow Memorial Park areas to contact them Det Ch Insp Thomas Willis said: "Detectives are pursuing a number of lines of enquiry and we are committed to identifying whoever is responsible and bringing them to justice."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club , or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! . . . . . Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. . . . . We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. Cost: £150 for the full course. Bursaries are available for those on lower income – please email learning@bandonthewall.org to arrange this.. . Spaces are limited – Book here . . . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Спектакль «Скамейка» в Лондоне | Алексей Панин | 29 ноября 2026 :: EventFirst Home double_arrow Events double_arrow Спектакль "Скамейка" On sale Спектакль "Скамейка" schedule 29 Nov 2026 Sunday, 19:00 location_on Logan Hall 20 Bedford Way, London WC1H 0AL balcony 6:00 pm gpp_maybe NO REFUNDS Buy On MAP Buy Tickets Logan Hall £30.00 Select Logan Hall £35.00 Select Logan Hall £40.00 Select Logan Hall £45.00 Select Logan Hall £50.00 Select Logan Hall £55.00 Select Logan Hall £60.00 Select Logan Hall £65.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £70.00 Select Logan Hall £80.00 Select Logan Hall £85.00 Sold Out Logan Hall £90.00 Select Друзья, а вы давно ощущали настоящую магию театра? 29 ноября 2026 года в Logan Hall — легендарная «Скамейка» с Алексеем Паниным. После аншлагов в Европе и США спектакль впервые приезжает в Лондон. 📍 University College London, Level 1, 20 Bedford Way, London WC1H 0AL 🕕 DOORS: 18:00 🕖 SHOW: 19:00 «Скамейка» — знаменитая пьеса, когда-то блистательно сыгранная Олегом Ефремовым и Татьяной Дорониной на сцене МХАТа, а затем покорившая театральные площадки по всему миру. Это история о мужчине и женщине. О случайной встрече, которая постепенно превращается в откровенный разговор — честный, смешной, ранимый и очень человеческий. О том моменте, когда между людьми исчезают роли и, наконец, становится невозможно притворяться. На сцене — Алексей Панин и Ольга Силина. Тонкая актерская игра, живая энергия и удивительно узнаваемая история, в которой каждый услышит что-то своё. “Скамейка” — спектакль, после которого хочется немного помолчать и еще долго думать о главном. Если вам не хватает настоящего театра — этот вечер нельзя пропустить. Количество билетов ограничено. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale | Bolton Sunday Car Boot Sale | Times, Prices & Info Skip to content 210+ UK car boot sales — find one near you this weekend Type your postcode or town to find sales near you Search car boot sales About This Car Boot Sale Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed open: 8 June 2026. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester United reporter in Trondheim Published 23 July 2026 Fifteen-year-old forward JJ Gabriel has been named in Manchester United 's senior squad for the first time for Friday's friendly against Rosenborg The youngster, who was the Under-18 Premier League player of the season last term despite only being 14 when the campaign began, is part of Michael Carrick's 25-man travelling party for the pre-season friendly in Trondheim Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, joins the squad that was beaten 1-0 by Wrexham in Finland last week, with striker Ethan Wheatley dropping out It means there is no place for 18-year-old Tynan Thompson, who has joined from Tottenham in an £8m deal. Striker Benjamin Sesko, goalkeeper Karl Darlow and defender Matthijs de Ligt are all ruled out by injury It had been expected Gabriel would play some part in United's pre-season this summer given the progress the Londoner has made through the club's youth system But should the winger feature in Norway to make his first senior appearance for the club, it will be the latest milestone in the teenager's career

evidence_packet.summary: Football Manchester United FC I was banished from Man United pre-season training – I made a mistake and the boss was right The brutal decision was fully supported by the player Comments Sport Mark Whiley 05:00, 27 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Luke Shaw has had a rollercoaster Man Luke
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC I was banished from Man United pre-season training – I made a mistake and the boss was right The brutal decision was fully supported by the player Comments Sport Mark Whiley 05:00, 27 Jul 2026 View 3 Images Luke Shaw has had a rollercoaster Man Luke Shaw is pushing to be Manchester United's starting left-back this season. But the 31-year-old has not has a smooth ride at Old Trafford and was once banished from pre-season training after reporting back out of shape In the summer of 2014, shortly after the World Cup, Shaw left then-United boss Louis van Gaal unhappy with his condition. The no-nonsense Dutch coach removed Shaw from regular training, with fitness staff handing him a bespoke programme to get him up to speed quickly Such a move would not have gone down well with many players. But with the then 19-year-old eager to prove himself ahead of his first full season at Old Trafford, he had no qualms with the treatment. He even endorsed Van Gaal's extreme measure Shaw said at the time: "Obviously, I have seen that [what Van Gaal said], and it's something I totally agree with. To play in this formation [wing-backs], you have to be really fit "I am fit but I am not at the high level he demands. I have got to get fitter to get up and down [the wing]. It's something I have got to work on. I want and need the staff to push me on so they can do what they want. It will only help me in the long run."
